{{Short description|Cohomology theory}}
In [[stable homotopy theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''Morava K-theory''' is one of a collection of [[cohomology theories]] introduced in [[algebraic topology]] by [[Jack Morava]] in unpublished preprints in the early 1970s. For every [[prime number]] ''p'' (which is suppressed in the notation), it consists of theories ''K''(''n'') for each nonnegative integer ''n'', each a [[ring spectrum (homotopy theory)|ring spectrum]] in the sense of [[homotopy theory]].   {{harvtxt|Johnson|Wilson|1975}} published the first account of the theories.

==Overview==

The theory ''K''(0) agrees with [[singular homology]] with rational coefficients, whereas ''K''(1) is a summand of mod-''p'' [[complex K-theory]]. The theory ''K''(''n'') has coefficient ring<ref>Lurie 2010, Lecture 22</ref>

:'''F'''<sub>''p''</sub>[''v''<sub>''n''</sub>,''v''<sub>''n''</sub><sup>&minus;1</sup>]

where ''v''<sub>''n''</sub> has degree 2(''p''<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1). In particular, Morava K-theory is periodic with this period, in much the same way that complex K-theory has period 2.

== Properties ==
* They have [[Künneth theorem|Künneth isomorphisms]] for arbitrary pairs of spaces: that is, for ''X'' and ''Y'' CW complexes, we have
:<math>K(n)_*(X \times Y) \cong K(n)_*(X) \otimes_{K(n)_*} K(n)_*(Y).</math>
* For every prime number <math>p</math> and every natural number <math>n\in\mathbb{N}</math>, Morava K-theory <math>K(n)</math> is a "field" in the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of [[ring spectrum (homotopy theory)|ring spectra]], meaning the [[graded ring]] <math>\pi_0K(n)</math> is even a graded field, meaning every nonzero homogeneous element in it is invertible.<ref>Lurie 2010, Lecture 24</ref> Therefore every [[module spectrum]] over <math>K(n)</math> is free, meaning it's a [[wedge sum|wedge]] of [[suspension (topology)|suspensions]] of <math>K(n)</math>.
* They are [[complex cobordism|complex oriented]] (at least after being periodified by taking the wedge sum of (''p''<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1) shifted copies), and the [[formal group]] they define has [[Formal group#The height of a formal group law|height]] ''n''.
* Every finite ''p''-local [[spectrum (homotopy theory)|spectrum]] ''X'' has the property that ''K''(''n'')<sub>∗</sub>(''X'') = 0 if and only if ''n'' is less than a certain number ''N'', called the [[Type (homotopy theory)|type]] of the spectrum ''X''. By a theorem of Devinatz&ndash;[[Michael J. Hopkins|Hopkins]]&ndash;Smith, every [[thick subcategory]] of the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of finite ''p''-local spectra is the subcategory of type-''n'' spectra for some ''n''.
* A connected [[Closed manifold|closed]] [[Spin manifold|spin]] 10-manifold is generalized oriented in second integral Morava K-theory <math>\widetilde{K}(2)</math> (for <math>p=2</math>) if and only if its seventh integral [[Stiefel–Whitney class]] <math>W_7</math> vanishes.

== K(n)-local spheres ==

For the [[sphere spectrum]] <math>\mathbb{S}</math> (with <math>\mathbb{S}_n=S^n</math>), its Bousfield localizations <math>L_{K(n)}\mathbb{S}</math> are also called <math>K(n)</math>-local spheres.
